decisive_items: A metal artifact reduction sequence MRI revealed a left periprosthetic soft‐tissue mass measuring 9 × 8 × 10 cm, without bony involvement or bone‐marrow edema.
Hip aspiration yielded 10,750 white cells/μL; all cultures were negative.
Serum cobalt and chromium levels were within normal limits.
response.rationale: The MRI shows a large periprosthetic soft-tissue mass without bone involvement, with negative cultures and normal metal ions, favoring a non-infectious, non-osteolytic local tissue reaction. R4 (ALTR) best fits the clinical and imaging picture; R6 is too specific to metal-on-metal, which is not the articulation here.

rejected.why: Negative cultures and normal metal ions argue against infection despite elevated WBC count.
Chronic inflammation is nonspecific and does not explain the mass or neurologic symptoms.
Bursitis cannot account for the large periprosthetic mass or progressive radicular pain.
ALTR associated with metal-on-metal is not applicable to a ceramic-on-ceramic bearing.
Explicitly no bony involvement or bone-marrow edema, contradicting osteolysis.
